segments.he: הַמְבַיֵּישׁ אֶת הַסּוֹמֵא וְכוּ׳. מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה; דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: סוֹמֵא – אֵין לוֹ בּוֹשֶׁת, וְכָךְ הָיָה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה פּוֹטֵר מֵחַיָּיבֵי גָלִיּוֹת, וּמֵחַיָּיבֵי מַלְקִיּוֹת, וּמֵחַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «One who humiliates a blind person» is liable to pay compensation. The Gemara comments: «The mishna is not in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda, as it is taught» in a baraita that «Rabbi Yehuda says: A blind person» who humiliated another «does not have» liability for «humiliation. And» in «this way Rabbi Yehuda deemed» a blind person «exempt from» being among «those liable to be exiled» for killing unintentionally, «and from» being among «those liable» to receive «lashes, and from» being among «those liable» to receive «court»-imposed «capital punishment,» if he transgresses a prohibition for which the Torah mandates one of these punishments.
